headline: Organic Sourdough Friendship Bread
intro: Slow-fermented, plant-based bread from a potato-flake starter, baked in a home kitchen in Roane County, Tennessee. Every loaf is made with organic ingredients.
payBody: The suggested price is $10 a loaf. That is what a loaf costs to make and bake, with a little left over to keep baking.
If that is more than you can do right now, pay what you can and take the bread home. No questions, no separate line.
If you can give a little more, it helps make bread available for someone who can't.
breadBody: The regular loaf is Amish-style friendship bread, the kind that starts from a shared starter and gets passed along. Mine is a potato-flake starter fed with water and sugar, which gives the bread a soft crumb and a gentle sweetness. It ferments slowly instead of rising on fast yeast.
I also bake a plain sourdough and a yeast bread. Ask which ones are coming out of the oven this week.
getSteps: Tell me which bread, how many, and the week you'd like it. I need a week's notice.
I bake it that week and let you know the day it's ready.
Meet me in Kingston to pick up. Pay what you can, and enjoy.
aboutBody: I'm Kathleen. I live in East Tennessee with my two boys, and I bake to feed people.

This started as a few loaves for friends and neighbors. The hope is that it grows into a small bakery where everyone pays what they can and the people who can give more help keep the oven going for the people who can't.
footerNote: Made in a home kitchen under Tennessee's cottage food rules. Not inspected by the Tennessee Department of Agriculture or Department of Health.

payCards.title: The suggested price
payCards.body: Covers the organic flour and sugar, the oven, and a little left over to keep baking.

payCards.title: If money is tight
payCards.body: Pay what you can and take the bread home. Same line, same bread, no questions.

payCards.title: If you have a little extra
payCards.body: Anything over $10 goes toward a loaf for someone who couldn't pay the full price.

faq.a: Yes, all of it. No dairy, no eggs, no honey. The friendship bread is flour, sugar, potato-flake starter, water, a little oil, and salt.
Everything is made with wheat flour in a home kitchen that also uses nuts, so I can't promise anything is free of them. Tell me what you need to avoid and I'll be honest about whether I can help.
A loaf keeps on the counter about three days in a bag or wrapped in a towel. Sliced and frozen, it keeps for a couple of months. Toast straight from the freezer.

faq.q: How far ahead should I ask?
faq.a: A week. The dough rises slowly and I bake to order, so I plan the week's loaves ahead and don't keep extras around.
Yes. Cash is easiest. Ask if you'd rather pay another way.

pickupNote: We'll settle on the spot and time when you ask. I don't deliver yet.
